vision_report.narrative_description: The chronological sequence of images from [EARLIEST] to [T-1] depicts a small indoor botanical setup consisting of two plants: a presumed Mexican Mint seedling in a black pot with soil and a sensor (P2), and a Money Plant cutting propagating in water within a white cup (Unmonitored). Throughout this period, both plants exhibited consistent signs of good health, maintaining turgid, appropriately colored foliage. The Mexican Mint seedling consistently showed two light green leaves, while the Money Plant cutting maintained a single, vibrant dark green leaf. Environmental conditions, particularly lighting and moisture, showed notable fluctuations. Images [EARLIEST], [T-4], [T-3], and [T-1] were taken under very dim, cool-spectrum light, while [T-2] was significantly brighter. Correspondingly, the soil in P2 appeared drier in [T-2] but was re-moistened by [T-1]. The water level in the Money Plant's cup also varied, appearing lower in [T-2] and replenished in [T-1]. These interventions (watering/replenishing) suggest active human monitoring and care, which successfully maintained plant health despite environmental shifts. However, the final image, labeled [CURRENT], presents a critical systemic anomaly: complete darkness. No plants, pots, or environmental details are discernible. This abrupt cessation of visual data renders any further botanical observation impossible and indicates a severe disruption to the monitoring system or the physical environment itself. All registered plants are considered 'Systemic Loss' from a visual monitoring perspective in this final state.
